column11: derived: JNJ turned 21.57% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 23.4% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: JNJ paid $5,540mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 2.07% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 2.11% to 0.04%. Restated at replacement capex: JNJ spent $13,799mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $8,728mm of depreciation and amortisation less amortisation of intangibles, 1.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 0.04% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: JNJ's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $6,000mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,500mm; 2024 instalment 2,000mm; 2025 instalment 2,500mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 27.17% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 31.91%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.74%. It was held at nil, but JNJ books $4,600mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000200406-26-000016), 4.88% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -4.74%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 JNJ's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,811mm, inventories up $3,901mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $6,344mm, a working capital build of $368mm, 0.14% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -4.74% to -4.88%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.2766 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3207 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -4.4065%.
